claims: Artemis II is a ~10-day crewed flight test of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft.
Artemis II is scheduled for April 2026.
Artemis II will fly four astronauts around the Moon and back.
Artemis II will test life-support systems.
Artemis II will test navigation.
Artemis II will test manual piloting.
Artemis II uses a "figure-8" free-return trajectory.
Artemis II passes within ~4,100 miles of the lunar surface.
On Day 1 of Artemis II, the SLS rocket lifts off from Kennedy Space Center.
On Day 1 of Artemis II, SLS places Orion in an initial high-Earth orbit.
On Day 1 of Artemis II, the crew performs systems checks.
On Day 1 of Artemis II, the crew performs manual proximity operations.
On Day 2 of Artemis II, Orion fires its engines to leave Earth's orbit.
On Day 2 of Artemis II, Orion enters a "free-return" trajectory toward the Moon.
During Days 3-6 of Artemis II, the spacecraft travels for roughly four days to reach the Moon.
During Days 3-6 of Artemis II, the spacecraft performs trajectory corrections.
During the Lunar Flyby of Artemis II, the spacecraft swings around the far side of the Moon.
During Days 7-10 of Artemis II, the crew returns to Earth.
During Days 7-10 of Artemis II, the crew performs a radiation shelter demo.
Artemis II splashes down in the Pacific Ocean.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight to test Orion’s life-support systems in deep space.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight to test Orion’s human-rated systems in deep space.
The crew of Artemis II will manually pilot the spacecraft near the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) to evaluate handling.
